claims.claim_summary: Unused details recede naturally without explicit importance scores or decay rules.
claims.claim_text_verbatim: Experience that remains unused continues to recede in detail through recursive consolidation, without separately assigned importance scores or time-based forgetting rules.

evidence_spans.source_text: Meanwhile, details of a routine placement episode recede through recursive consolidation (Fig. 7).
These thresholds control when context is consolidated, rather than assigning importance or decay scores to individual memories.

claims.label: partially_supported
claims.claim_summary: Use and disuse dynamics unify memory recall with continuous learning and capability expansion.
claims.claim_text_verbatim: This natural dynamic of use and disuse unifies the recovery of past experience with learning that deepens what the agent knows, refines how it acts, and expands what it can accomplish.

evidence_spans.source_text: Disabling recall on the same post-ingestion MemoryAgentBench 64k snapshot reduces accuracy from 41.0% to 27.0%. Access to underlying evidence therefore improves reasoning beyond what the consolidated context alone supports.
ALFWorld success remains near perfect, but mean actions increase from 9.62 to 11.74, and episode-start context grows from 19.7k to 50.7k tokens in the inspected stream.

Supplementation occurs in 28.4% of matched-call transitions and 11.7% of differing-call transitions, compared with 0.9% of transitions without detected use. Concrete-value updates are more frequent when the reference specifies a different call (3.4%) than when the call matches (0.3%) or no use is detected (0.1%).

These associations connect subsequent knowledge changes to intervening work and feedback, without establishing that use alone causes the changes. Most items without detected use remain unchanged (95.8%), so these adjacent-consolidation statistics do not establish general fading of unused knowledge.
